record.original_question: If a non-periodic bi-infinite word w has k disjoint X-factorizations for a finite set X of words with k <= |X|, must the combinatorial rank satisfy r(X) <= |X|-k+1?

evidence.quote: Let X be a finite set of words, andw be a non-periodic bi-infinite word. Assume that w possesses k disjoint X-factorizations, with k<=| X|. Is it true that we have r(X)<=| X|- k + 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $A^*$ denote the free monoid of finite words over $A$. A bi-infinite word over $A$ is a sequence $w = \cdots a_{-2}a_{-1}a_0 a_1 a_2 \cdots$ with $a_i \in A$ for all $i \in \mathbb{Z}$. Such a word $w$ is called periodic if there is an integer $p \geq 1$ such that $a_{i+p} = a_i$ for all $i \in \mathbb{Z}$, and non-periodic otherwise.

Given a finite set $X \subseteq A^*\setminus\{\varepsilon\}$ of nonempty words, an $X$-factorization of a bi-infinite word $w$ is a factorization $w = \cdots x_{-1} x_0 x_1 \cdots$ with each $x_i \in X$, specified together with the sequence of cutting positions $(p_i)_{i \in \mathbb{Z}} \subset \mathbb{Z}$ between consecutive factors. Two $X$-factorizations of $w$ are called disjoint if their sets of cutting positions are disjoint.

The combinatorial rank $r(X)$ of $X$ is defined as
$$r(X) = \min\{\,|F| : F \subseteq A^* \text{ and } X \subseteq F^*\,\}.$$

Question: Suppose $X \subseteq A^*$ is a finite set of nonempty words and $w$ is a non-periodic bi-infinite word over $A$ that admits $k$ pairwise disjoint $X$-factorizations, where $k \leq |X|$. Must the combinatorial rank satisfy
$$r(X) \leq |X| - k + 1\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The case $k=2$ is established by the defect theorem for bi-infinite words (Karhumäki–Maňuch–Plandowski), which yields $r(X) \leq |X|-1$. The general statement for arbitrary $k \leq |X|$ appears in the WORDS open-problem collection and no source found in the search confirms its resolution; the status is therefore unknown to this assistant.

status_evidence.title: A defect theorem for bi-infinite words
status_evidence.snippet: If a nonperiodic bi-infinite word has two X-factorizations, then the combinatorial rank of X is at most card(X)-1.
status_evidence.claim: The k=2 case is known: two disjoint X-factorizations of a non-periodic bi-infinite word imply r(X) <= |X|-1.

status_evidence.title: On defect effect of bi-infinite words
status_evidence.snippet: Defect-type results for bi-infinite words with multiple X-factorizations.
status_evidence.claim: Background results on the defect effect for bi-infinite words underlying the conjecture.
